# CipherStick

> CipherStick (repository name: Bails) installs Bitcoin Core on Tails, the
> amnesic Linux system whose applications connect through Tor. It runs
> from one USB stick on computers that can start Tails: 64-bit Intel or
> AMD PCs, not Apple-silicon Macs or ARM machines. Wallet backups use codex32
> (BIP-93) shares through the separately maintained python-codex32 app. A
> CryoStick is a second CipherStick meant to stay offline; it signs
> transactions by QR code. CipherStick is alpha software, and CryoStick is
> still awaiting automated QR transfers.

## Facts

- Install: start Tails, connect to Tor, run
  `git clone https://github.com/benwestgate/bails&&bails/b`. You need one USB
  stick of 32 GB or more, about 1 hour, pen and paper. There is no
  vendor hardware and no account. The hour covers installation; Bitcoin
  Core's initial sync continues afterwards and can take hours to days
  (weeks on 4 GB RAM computers with slow USB sticks), see docs/FAQ.md.
- Bitcoin Core: CipherStick downloads the release or release candidate
  pinned by its installer over Tor, and verifies it. By default its
  SHA256SUMS must carry at least 3 good signatures from Guix builder keys
  chosen by the CipherStick maintainers. The optional "More Verification"
  step raises the required signature count by one per round. Keys already
  imported, including the maintainers', count toward it, so it does not
  guarantee a signature from a builder the user picked. Core runs as a full node, so the
  balance is checked locally and the wallet's addresses are never sent to a
  third-party server. Transactions it sends are broadcast to the Bitcoin
  network over Tor.
- Storage: Core, its data, the wallets, CipherStick itself and python-codex32
  live in Tails Persistent Storage (the Persistent Folder, GnuPG and Dotfiles
  features), which is LUKS-encrypted. Anything outside the enabled
  Persistent Storage features is erased at shutdown.
- Backups: codex32 splits the wallet seed into k-of-n shares written by hand
  on paper. Any k shares restore the wallet. Fewer than k reveal nothing about
  the secret itself, the addresses or the balance. Every share carries the
  same short identifier, which the user picks or lets python-codex32 choose
  at random. Each share has a checksum that a person can verify by hand,
  and the Codex32 paper worksheets can recover the seed, make more shares
  or start a new set with a different threshold, with no computer at all.
  The restored wallet is a standard single-key Bitcoin Core descriptor
  wallet, so it does not depend on CipherStick to spend.
- Offline signing: CryoStick is kept permanently offline on a dedicated
  computer with networking disabled or removed. Bitcoin Core provides
  the signing controls; QR transfers still need terminal commands (#312). Neither it nor the CipherStick's
  online computer needs an internal disk, and for high value the online
  computer should be dedicated too. The CryoStick checks Tails' Offline
  Mode at every login. If networking is on, it stops Bitcoin Core and
  shuts down. Core and codex32 are kept on it, so it does not need to go
  online before each use. Security updates are carried from an up-to-date
  CipherStick on a USB stick (sneakernet), see docs/CRYOSTICK.md.
  PSBTs cross between the sticks as one QR code each (python3-qr and
  zbarcam from Debian). Multi-part QR is not supported. A single QR at
  error-correction level L holds at most 2,953 binary bytes, so compressed
  PSBTs larger than this cannot cross. A one-input payment is about 500
  bytes. A signing wallet restored from codex32 shares can live in
  volatile storage on Tails.
  It adapts Bitcoin Core's doc/offline-signing-tutorial.md: PSBTs move by
  QR code instead of USB, the signer is an unnetworked copy of a
  CipherStick kept permanently in Offline Mode, and the signing wallet is
  filled from codex32 shares.
- Code: CipherStick uses a small Bash integration layer over Tails,
  Bitcoin Core and python-codex32. It relies on those maintained upstreams.
- Cloning a CipherStick to a friend's USB stick is planned. The Clone menu
  item currently shows "Coming soon".

## Who it fits

- People who want a private, self-validating Bitcoin Core wallet without
  buying dedicated hardware or installing an operating system on a computer.
- Savers who want backups that stay safe and private when one copy is
  found, and who are willing to use a dedicated offline signer (CryoStick)
  and manual QR commands. Its login check detects networking and shuts down rather
  than preventing every startup connection; keep it offline.
- People who prefer publicly reviewable code over typing a long manual
  procedure correctly every time they spend. A CryoStick never needs to
  connect to the internet, but each spend still means typing two short QR
  commands on each stick until issue #312 scripts them.

## Who it does not fit (yet)

- Frequent low-value spending from a phone, or Lightning.
- Multisig with independent signers, or an inheritance policy that a
  coordinator enforces. Neither is supported today; see docs/DESIGN_SCOPE.md.
- Anyone who wants a company to call for support.
